title: Fix pagination off-by-one and clamping
prompt:
Bug report: `paginate()` in `pager.py` returns wrong results. Users see page 1 showing the second page of results, the last page coming back empty, wrong page counts when the item count is not a multiple of the page size, and nothing sensible for an empty list or for a page number past the end. Fix `pager.py` so it matches the specification below.

Visible tests (a partial set; some of them currently fail): `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`

Specification of `paginate(items, page, per_page)`:
- `items` is a list. `page` is 1-based (page 1 is the first page). `per_page` is the page size.
- It returns a dict with exactly these keys:
  - `items`: the slice of `items` on the returned page, as a new list (the input list is never modified)
  - `page`: the page number actually returned (see clamping below)
  - `per_page`: the page size that was passed in
  - `total`: `len(items)`
  - `pages`: ceil(total / per_page), but never less than 1 (an empty list has exactly one, empty, page)
  - `has_next`: True when a later page exists (`page < pages`)
  - `has_prev`: True when an earlier page exists (`page > 1`)
- An out-of-range `page` (below 1 or above `pages`) is clamped into [1, pages] instead of raising. The returned `page` is the clamped value, and `items`, `has_next` and `has_prev` describe that clamped page.
- `per_page < 1` raises `ValueError`.
- Only lists need to be supported.
